newsitem.title: UK: Siemens UK unit predicts profit recovery.
newsitem.headline: Siemens UK unit predicts profit recovery.

text.p: Siemens Holdings Plc, the British arm of diversified German engineering and technology group Siemens AG, said on Thursday it expects to bounce back from sluggish profits by the end of 1996/97 and go on to beat an internal group profit target thereafter.

Juergen Gehrels, chief executive of the wholly-owned company, told an annual media presentation that although 1995/96 had been a disappointing year, characterised by "significant price erosion in many businesses", he saw good prospects.

"It is only the mix of businesses that right now leads to a rather depressed earnings situation," he said, explaining that two years of start-up costs for a 1.1 billion stg semiconductor plant from 1995 to 1997 would start paying off after this year.
"Once North Tyneside (the silicon wafer factory) is up and running I see no reason why we should not exceed the internal rate of return set by Siemens AG," he said.
Siemens AG wants its units to achieve a 15 percent return on equity and Gehrels said all his firm's well-established UK businesses exceeded that rate last year.

However, as well as the factory costs, last year's profits were also hit by an acquisition and ensuing reorgansation in its new business telecommunications arm, as well as higher than expected startup investments in air traffic control systems. As a result, the company calculated that its overall UK profitability rate fell to about 1.5 percent of turnover in 1995/96 from 2.0 percent of turnover in 1994/95, he said.
"Overall, our return on equity was about 12 percent," finance director Bernd Euler told reporters.
Growth boosted by billings for two power stations should help raise turnover in 1996/97 towards 2.3 billion stg, Gehrels said, after it rose 16.4 percent to 1.5 billion stg in 1995/96.
Predicting a continued turnover growth rate of between 15 and 24 percent for the next five years, he said Siemens Plc aimed to be a 4.0 billion stg company by the year 2000 or 2001.
